quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 results (CEO Benoit Coquart / CFO Franck Lemery): sales up 17.4% excluding currency effects - organic growth of +9.8%, driven by data centers and energy-transition offerings, and +6.9% from acquisitions; currency effect -3.7% (around -1.5% for the full year at June 2026 average rates). Like-for-like by region: Europe -2.4% in a contrasted building market; North and Central America +24.2%, driven by data-center and energy-transition solutions in the U.S.; rest of the world +2.3%, with significant growth in India, Australia and several other Asian countries, China soft and Middle East sales up. Adjusted operating margin 20.8%; net profit EUR 698 million, up 11.2% (corporate income tax rate 27.5%); free cash flow EUR 488 million, 9% of sales. CEO: price effect +2.9% in H1 (Q1 +2.1%, Q2 +3.6%) against purchase-price inflation of +3% (Q1 +2%, Q2 +4%).
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 sales +17.4% ex-FX (organic +9.8%, acquisitions +6.9%); North and Central America +24.2% LFL; adjusted operating margin 20.8%; net profit EUR 698 million (+11.2%)

quarterly_data.signal: Raised full-year 2026 targets (CEO Benoit Coquart): sales growth excluding currency effects of +16% to +19% (previously +10% to +15%), comprising organic growth of +8% to +10% (previously +4% to +7%) and growth through acquisitions of around +8% (previously +6% to +8%); adjusted operating margin after acquisitions of 20.5% to 21% of sales, unchanged. The guidance assumes data-center like-for-like growth of 25%-30% and low single-digit growth for the rest of the business, with no sharp building-market rebound in the U.S. or Europe. CFO: the acquisition parameter is based only on deals already announced ('it could be 7.7, it could be 8.2'); full-year free cash flow should be the usual 13%-15% of sales as working capital (around 14% of sales at end-H1 versus a typical 12%) normalizes. CEO: full-year price effect up to around +3% against purchase-price inflation of a little more than +4%; restructuring around 2025's EUR 65 million (EUR 33 million in H1 versus EUR 34 million a year earlier); tariffs had no material impact in H1 and margins are 'clean'.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026: sales +16% to +19% ex-FX; organic +8% to +10%; acquisitions around +8%; adjusted operating margin 20.5% to 21%

quarterly_data.signal: Data centers (CEO Benoit Coquart): data-center organic growth was above +30% in H1, stronger in North America, and data centers now account for 32% of Legrand's revenue. Full-year data-center organic growth is now expected at 25% to 30% (close to 20% guided three months earlier), implying 20% to 30% in H2: 'the pace is not slowing down. We have very, very solid orders.' The fastest-growing product families (50% to 100%) are cooling, testing, commissioning and part of the powertrain. Orders run for delivery in 2026, some in 2027 and 2028, and on some longer-lead-time businesses a few orders for 2028 and sometimes 2029, but the CEO does not treat the backlog as visibility; he tracks the tens of gigawatts announced for 2027, 2028 and beyond, with potentially EUR 2 billion-EUR 3 billion of Legrand sales per gigawatt, and hyperscalers' raised capex plans. Europe: no benefit yet in 2026 from European data-center announcements (late-cycle sales; three to five years from announcement to opening), although Legrand could sell more dollars per megawatt in Europe than in the U.S.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 data-center organic growth above +30%; 32% of revenue; FY2026 data-center organic growth 25% to 30%; EUR 2 billion-EUR 3 billion of sales per gigawatt

quarterly_data.signal: Operations (CEO Benoit Coquart): the main operating challenge is coping with data-center hypergrowth - optimizing the supply chain, speeding up new-product development, shipping on time and sending people on site for installation and commissioning - which adds costs ('Sometimes you are doing plane instead of a ship'). Productivity: volumes were up close to 7% in H1 with like-for-like headcount flat. Competition: no increase in competitive intensity in data centers; new entrants have bought assets mainly in liquid cooling.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 volume up close to 7% with flat like-for-like headcount

quarterly_data.signal: 800 V DC / LVDC (CEO Benoit Coquart): Legrand is working on the full hybrid AC-DC architecture including the sidecar ('we are not late compared to what we can see on the market') and on full LVDC. Base scenario: hybrid AC-DC could represent maybe 10% or 20% of new IT loads by 2030, and full LVDC at best 1% or 2%. '100% of the orders everybody gets today ... are based on the traditional AC architecture', including orders for delivery in 2027 and 2028. Legrand has all the technical building blocks of a sidecar, internally or through contract manufacturing and subcontracting; it is a UPS player outside data centers but not inside them, so the sidecar is 'mostly additional value' with 'almost nothing to lose'. CEO: neither OCP nor 800 V DC architectures will concentrate the market in a few players; they favour incumbents with hyperscaler relationships and broad catalogues.
quarterly_data.figure: hybrid AC-DC maybe 10%-20% of new IT loads by 2030; full LVDC at best 1%-2%

quarterly_data.signal: Acquisitions (CEO Benoit Coquart): seven acquisitions announced so far in 2026, including one in Finland on the day of the call, all in the energy and digital transition, with combined annual revenue of around EUR 450 million. The aim of the recent U.S. deals is a significant position in critical power across the powertrain - containerized turbine gensets, medium- and low-voltage gear, busway, busbar, testing and commissioning - with most acquired companies having about half their sales in data centers. Avtron (load banks) helps test loads and liquid-cooling systems as rack density rises; Girtz supplies gas- or diesel-powered genset modules usable as a main power source; Kratos supplies pre-mounted critical-power skids, integrating third-party AC or DC breakers into engineered panels, and the CEO confirmed the objective of growing it 20%, 30%, 40% per year; module units include Tecnica (Colombia), TES (Ireland) and the newly acquired SRS (Malaysia), which builds power skids and modules. The pace will slow from almost a deal a month, with a pipeline of 350 companies tracked, mostly EUR 50 million-EUR 100 million businesses; the CEO does not expect 100% or even 80% of future acquisitions to be data-center related.
quarterly_data.figure: seven acquisitions in 2026 to date, combined annual revenue around EUR 450 million; pipeline of 350 companies

quarterly_data.signal: Non-data-center business and margins (CEO Benoit Coquart / CFO Franck Lemery): building markets in the U.S. and Europe remain unsupportive; energy-transition families (transformers, circuit breakers, measurement, load shedding) grow a few points faster than essential products, and in Europe the energy-transition business grows while essentials decline. U.S. residential is less than 10% of U.S. sales and depressed, with no office rebound; U.S. non-data-center growth comes from health, education, infrastructure, industry and transportation verticals. H1 adjusted operating margin fell 20 basis points (half acquisitions, half organic): gross margin -130 basis points mostly from acquisitions, SG&A +90 basis points, other +20 basis points. Europe's margin of 18% is close to 5 points below last year, mainly from SG&A carrying central costs and restructuring; Legrand is closing four sites in France. CEO on the long-term data-center growth rate: 'it won't be 30% or 40%', with 10%, 15% or 20% open for discussion.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 adjusted operating margin -20 basis points; Europe margin 18%; four French sites closing
